papers.title: Zeroth persistent homology of ground-state correlations at clean and disordered quantum transitions
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields exhibits a continuous critical point, a mixed-order transition line and, with quenched disorder, an infinite-disorder fixed point and reentrant order. Using exact free-fermion solutions and the density-matrix renormalization group, we examine what the zeroth persistent homology of staggered ground-state correlations adds to conventional responses. Its barcode records the merge scales of the single-linkage hierarchy, and the maximum of its persistence-landscape velocity defines a threshold-free pseudocritical point. This point locates the clean critical point and the mixed-order line with an accuracy comparable to conventional responses. In the reentrant regime, the global velocity misplaces the entry, which is recovered only by restricting the filtration to the ordering scale, and none of the tested estimators locates the exit. A domain wall forced by the boundary conditions suppresses the disorder-averaged reentrant lobe. For individual disordered realizations, the labelled merge tree recovers most strong-disorder renormalization-group clusters, including noncontiguous ones missed by lattice-restricted hierarchies, with increasing agreement at stronger disorder. This information resides in the full correlation matrix, while zeroth homology provides a stable, threshold-free hierarchy.

papers.title: Selecting and verifying load-bearing periodic cells for elastic-wave band gaps with numerical acceptance checks
papers.abstract: A lattice mount must be stiff enough to support equipment and block vibration over a specified frequency range. Fast simulations help rank designs, but their errors can lead to a wrong acceptance decision. We present AMM (AgenticMetamaterials), an open-source Python tool that searches repeating cubic cells for targets on stiffness, the fraction of the cell that is solid, and band gaps. A complete band gap is an interval with no elastic-wave propagation in any direction. A separate checker allows for changes as the simulation grid gets finer. For gaps, it also tests for modes at sampled wave directions and wavelengths, so it can miss modes between samples. In 1,500 near-threshold tests of stiffness and solid fraction, the checker accepted 454 of 750 claims supported by the reference and none of the 750 false claims. Using the finest grid estimate alone accepted 42 false claims. In an independent finite-element comparison on ten new cells built from cubes joined by bars, the checker accepted one of two true gap claims and left all 17 false claims undecided. The reference could not classify the remaining claim. The protocol required every reported edge to err on the side of a narrower gap. The checker failed this test when it placed one upper edge too high, even though it left that thin-bar cell's claim undecided. Separating search from acceptance shows which targets the evidence supports and where a calculation needs further refinement.

papers.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
papers.abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.

papers.title: Bounding Freedom of Choice via Causal Network Embeddings
papers.abstract: Standard Bell inequalities rely on measurement independence, the assumption that measurement settings are perfectly decoupled from the source of correlations. We demonstrate that embedding Bell scenarios into larger causal networks naturally overcomes this limitation. This embedding yields experimentally accessible lower and upper bounds on measurement dependence, the incompatibility of which certifies nonclassicality directly from data, without assuming a priori freedom of choice. We formulate a general linear-programming framework to systematically derive these measurement-dependence consistency (MDC) Bell inequalities. By bypassing standard non-convexity hurdles, this approach significantly outperforms existing techniques in computational simplicity and noise robustness. Finally, we reveal that genuine quantum nonlocality can be certified even for correlations exceeding the Tsirelson bound, and demonstrate our method's broad applicability to multi-outcome and multipartite Bell tests.

papers.title: Lost in the Bins: Treatment Effects with Discretized Covariates
papers.abstract: Mean independence restrictions are widely used to identify average treatment effects, but the covariates used to formulate these restrictions are often observed or used in coarsened form. This paper shows that mean independence conditional on a finely measured covariate need not hold after the covariate is replaced by a coarsened version. Coarsening can therefore change the identifying content of the comparison rather than only the precision of estimation. I characterize the resulting coarsening bias for the ATT and ATE. For the ATT, the bias is driven by within-cell composition in untreated potential outcomes. For the ATE, an additional treatment effect heterogeneity term appears. I then introduce $c$-mean dependence, a nonparametric relaxation of exact mean independence at the coarsened level, and derive sharp bounds for average treatment effects. The parameter $c$ determines how far comparisons may extend across neighboring values of the coarsened covariate. I propose sample analogue estimators and bootstrap inference procedures for the resulting bound functions. In an application to voluntary military service using data from Angrist (1998), positive effects on early earnings, which primarily reflect military pay, hold even under the weakest form of $c$-mean dependence, whereas the evidence on later effects on civilian earnings is inconclusive once mean independence is relaxed.

papers.title: Source Assignment: Hardness, Approximation, and Parameterized Algorithms
Semiparametric Inference for Marginal Win Odds with Censored Time-to-Event Outcomes
papers.abstract: Win statistics provide clinically interpretable measures for comparing treatment groups with prioritized composite outcomes, but efficient covariate-adjustment methods for win statistics with right censored time-to-event outcomes remain limited. We develop a semiparametric framework for marginal win probability and win odds with prioritized time-to-event outcomes, including semi-competing risks, while also accommodating scalar survival outcomes as a special case. The estimand compares independent draws from the marginal distributions of the potential outcomes under treatment and control, which preserves a marginal causal interpretation. We derive the efficient influence function under conditional independent censoring, allowing censoring to depend on baseline covariates and predictable event history. The resulting cross-fitted one-step estimator incorporates covariate adjustment and censoring martingale augmentation, allows flexible estimation of nuisance parameters, and attains the semiparametric efficiency bound under suitable conditions on consistency and convergence rate of nuisance parameters. Simulation studies show that the estimator has small bias, accurate standard error estimation and confidence interval coverage, and substantial efficiency gain relative to the inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW) estimator. An application to a randomized breast cancer trial comparing tamoxifen combined with radiotherapy against tamoxifen alone demonstrates improved precision, with an approximately 25\% reduction in estimated variance at five years.

papers.title: Making Poisson σ again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $\sigma$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $\Sigma$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = \Sigma \times G \to \Sigma$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,\omega)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,\Pi)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = \Sigma \times M \to \Sigma$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $\Sigma$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,\Pi)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $\omega$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

papers.title: A Multi-Prover Interactive Protocol for Certification of Resolution Refutations
Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference weighs competing explanations of noisy data by sampling from a posterior distribution, a task that deterministic hardware performs only by simulating randomness. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) supply this randomness physically, but the few hardware networks of p-bits built so far use inorganic devices, address optimization or learning, and are judged without reference to the spread expected from finite sampling. Here we report a probabilistic computer built from solution-processed conjugated-polymer memristors. Four polymer p-bits, tracked online for drift and coupled in a closed Gibbs-sampling loop, sample competing, degenerate and cooperative posteriors over sixteen states with statistics that fall within the range of ideal p-bits, both in their distribution and in their autocorrelation, without any parameter fitted to the target. This agreement extends to new simulated sensor readings whose outcome was predicted before each run, including readings that point away from the true answer. Reprogrammed in software, the same circuit and controller reproduces the invertible AND gate of earlier p-bit networks, with its temperature fixed in advance rather than fitted. Polymer p-bits thus open a route to printed, large-area probabilistic computers that infer alongside their sensors.

Turbulence Properties of Corotating Interaction Regions at 1 AU: a Comprehensive Superposed Epoch Analysis
papers.abstract: We perform a comprehensive superposed epoch analysis (SEA) of more than 200 corotating interaction regions (CIRs) using WIND spacecraft observations at 1 AU. The stream interfaces are identified by Minimum Variance Analysis (MVA), and turbulence properties are evaluated using wavelet transforms over a wide range of temporal scales. The analysis of normalized cross helicity ($\sigma_c$) and normalized residual energy ($\sigma_r$) reveals distinct turbulence behaviors across frequencies. The spectral indices of both magnetic and velocity fluctuations smoothly transition from steeper in the slow wind to shallower in the fast wind, while a localized steepening of the velocity spectra near the interface indicates enhanced dissipation due to compression. Across broad frequency bands, $\sigma_c$ shows a clear dip at the stream interface, signifying increased inward Alfvén wave energy, whereas $\sigma_r$ displays a peak-valley-peak structure mainly driven by large-scale velocity shear. In lower-frequency ranges, velocity shear artificially enhances velocity fluctuation energy, producing strong peaks in $\sigma_r$, while higher-frequency ranges show a smooth increase of $\sigma_r$ from slow wind to fast wind. Nearly half of the analyzed CIRs are accompanied by a heliospheric current sheet (HCS), with many HCSs closely aligned with the stream interface, suggesting an intrinsic link between the two structures. Our findings offer valuable clues for reconciling discrepancies among earlier observational and simulation studies, and provide new insight into how compression and velocity shear modulate solar wind turbulence near CIRs.

Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Periodic Solids. I. Hydrogen and p-block Elements from Boron to Chlorine
papers.abstract: We present the cc-pVXZ-s series (X = D, T, and Q) of correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for solids, covering hydrogen and the p-block elements from boron to chlorine. The series includes basis sets of consistent quality for the all-electron potential and for various pseudopotentials and effective core potentials commonly used in periodic calculations. Our design combines Dunning's construction of the molecular cc-pVXZ series with a revised material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO) algorithm for improved numerical performance. MCAO regularizes standard atomic optimization to suppress overly diffuse basis functions and ensure numerical stability in a set of reference solids. Benchmarks against standard cc-pVXZ calculations for molecules and plane-wave calculations for periodic solids establish the accuracy, transferability, and numerical stability of cc-pVXZ-s in both mean-field and correlated wavefunction calculations and confirm reliable extrapolation to the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit. As an application, we use all-electron cc-pVXZ-s to compute basis-set-converged lattice constants, bulk moduli, and cohesive energies for 7 bulk semiconductors. Using a hierarchy of correlated wavefunction methods up to local coupled cluster with singles, doubles, and perturbative triples [CCSD(T)], we find systematic convergence toward experimental bulk moduli and cohesive energies, while a small systematic overestimation of lattice constants suggests potential limitations in the approximate finite-size treatment. This work provides a foundation for the further development of systematically convergent Gaussian basis sets for periodic calculations.

Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
papers.abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

Experimental Investigation of Hypersonic Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction Dynamics Using Plasma-Generated Disturbances
papers.abstract: The unsteady dynamics of a transitional 3D shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction (SWBLI) are investigated using pulsed plasma disturbances on a cone-slice-ramp geometry in the Boeing/AFOSR Mach-6 Quiet Tunnel. Nanosecond-duration repetitively pulsed spark discharges introduce disturbances which convect through the interaction, causing transient turbulent breakdown in the reattaching shear layer. The unsteady behavior of the separation bubble is characterized using schlieren imaging, and natural broadband unsteadiness is observed in the form of large-scale shock and separation flapping at frequencies below 1500 Hz ($Sr_L< 0.25$). Disturbance packets are introduced at a range of perturbation frequencies and generally induce shear layer oscillations; however, perturbation frequencies below the natural cutoff frequency ($f\approx 1500$ $\mathrm{Hz}$) yield fluctuations with significantly larger amplitudes than those above this frequency. Phase-averaged schlieren images reveal that the disturbances cause a decrease in shear layer height immediately after inducing turbulent breakdown around the reattachment point, with this displacement beginning downstream and moving upstream. The shear layer's response to this displacement is consistent with that of an under-damped dynamic system with a preferred oscillation frequency; the measured frequency of the oscillatory response to external perturbation ($f = 1464$ Hz) is also the approximate cutoff frequency of the natural broadband unsteadiness. Furthermore, the relationship between perturbation frequency and oscillation amplitude resembles that of a low-pass filter, with a cutoff frequency that is within 5\% of the measured oscillator frequency. These experimental findings support the theory that the cutoff frequency for the SWBLI's frequency-selective amplification is tied to the time scale of the weakly damped global mode.

papers.title: Identification of Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel class of econometric models, called Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models. It is based on the discrete choice rational inattention model of Matvejka and McKay (2015) with additive unobserved heterogeneity incorporated. We show that some of the systematic components of the primitives of the model are nonparametrically identified even if the distributions of unobserved variables and the prior of decision makers are both unknown to the Econometrician. If additional information about the prior is known to the Econometrician, even stronger identification results become available.

Harmonic structure and parametric prediction of instantaneous power in oscillating foils
papers.abstract: A closed-form model is developed to predict the instantaneous lift, pitching moment, and power of an oscillating-foil energy harvester directly from its kinematic input. Such foils extract renewable power from moving water through sinusoidal heaving and pitching. However, due to their large-amplitude motion and vortex-dominated dynamics, classical unsteady aerodynamics cannot accurately predict the time-dependent force and power generation. To generate the model, 405 two-dimensional simulations are computed which vary heave amplitude, pitch amplitude, and frequency, representing the energy harvesting kinematic parameter space. The lift and pitching moment are decomposed into odd Fourier harmonics, and each Fourier coefficient is regressed on sixteen physics-based polynomial terms derived from the kinematic, power, and energy scalings. The regression is performed in two Ridge steps, one for attribution and one for the deployable predictor. The attribution shows that the first harmonic, which contains the mean power, depends on the motion amplitudes. The higher harmonics respond nonlinearly to the frequency, which determines the number and timing of the vortex shedding. The model recovers the cycle-averaged power with a leave-one-out $R^2$ of $0.98$, and reproduces the instantaneous lift with a median peak error of $9\%$ and a median phase error below $1\%$ of the period. The harmonic order of the response counts the discrete vortex events in each stroke, as confirmed by the wake visualization. The model's analytical expression for time-dependent force and power can be utilized as a fast and accurate alternative to high-fidelity simulations, specifically targeting device design and array optimization of oscillating foils.

papers.title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
papers.abstract: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

papers.title: Beyond Ground States: Learning Many-Body Hamiltonians for p-Bit Invertible Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Probabilistic-bit (p-bit) invertible logic encodes a Boolean relation as an energy whose ground states are its legal assignments, computing in any direction by sampling. Traditional constructions target ground-state membership and a wide minimum energy gap, yet finite-time samplers traverse excited states. We cast Hamiltonian design as inverse statistical mechanics: fit an energy with interactions up to order four whose Gibbs law approaches uniformity on each clamp case's legal states, under a gap floor keeping every legal state below every illegal one. Constrained maximum likelihood with pruning and refitting fits terms from a fixed pool, and every delivered energy is audited exactly on all cases. Each energy is scored by time to a verified solution under restarts with its best of nine tuned samplers. In underdetermined modes, learned multipliers factor in 0.55, 0.44, 0.52 and 0.46 [0.38, 0.56] of the hand-written encodings' updates from 4x4 to 7x7, faster within every family below 7x7 at no resolved work penalty; learned adders solve the reverse mode in 0.71 of the updates at 8 bits and about a quarter at 24 and 32 bits, at 0.55 of the work at 32 bits. At 5x5 under equal pool, budget and floor, a gap-maximizing fit reaches 0.79 [0.73, 0.88] in updates and 1.26 in work against the hand-written encoding, while likelihood fitting takes 0.55 [0.46, 0.58] and 0.58 [0.48, 0.61] of the gap fit's updates and work. Rounding coefficients to the narrowest exact integer words tested, we run both energies at each pair's common word on one FPGA color-sweep SSA core, bit-exact with software: learned multipliers take 0.41 of the hand-written encoding's cycles at 4x4 and 0.057 [0.045, 0.068] at 7x7, at up to 2.4 times its lookup tables. The method requires only a circuit's legal assignments; in determined modes, hand-written encodings take less work, and from 12 bits on the adder fewer updates.

papers.title: VIDE 2.0: Robust, Scalable Void Finding for Extremely Large Galaxy Surveys
papers.abstract: Current and future spectroscopic and photometric galaxy surveys will deliver unprecedented numbers of galaxies, with expected counts in the tens of millions. To answer the computational challenges posed by these surveys, in this paper we present VIDE 2.0, a significantly improved and enhanced void finding algorithm and analysis pipeline based on VIDE. Leveraging the parameter-free identification of voids via a Voronoi tessellation and watershed scheme, we implement a robust mechanism for handling survey boundaries and incompleteness without relying on vast numbers of boundary particles. This new method identifies edge galaxies and flags voids contaminated by their presence. The mechanism is fully deterministic, producing bit-for-bit reproducible catalogs from identical inputs. An automatic rule for setting the mask resolution renders the entire pipeline parameter-free. Combined with other performance enhancements to the underlying VIDE engine, we find significant ($>100\times$) speedups and a dramatic reduction in memory usage compared to previous versions: a 12-million-galaxy DESI Y1-class mock catalog now completes in roughly 15 minutes on a single laptop, where VIDE 1.0 could not run a catalog of even $10^6$ galaxies on the same hardware. We are also able to identify voids existing closer to survey boundaries via deterministic per-void contamination flags, maximizing their statistical potential. We exercise the upgraded pipeline on two large mock suites (MultiDark-Patchy DR12 and AbacusSummit DESI Y1 ELG), demonstrating converged cosmic-variance covariances for the void number function, the void-galaxy cross-correlation, and the void ellipticity distribution -- key ingredients for Stage IV void cosmology. VIDE 2.0 is now well suited to handle large numbers of galaxies in mock and real observations, and ready to tackle the challenges of future campaigns.

papers.title: Reconstructing Fine-grained Memory Reuse Structure in GPU Kernels
General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near )a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter $\bar{\kappa} \equiv r_s\Delta y^2/r^3$, where $r$ is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, $r_s$ is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and $\Delta y$ is the mesoscale length.

papers.title: Fragility of Aeolian Ripples
papers.abstract: Sand surfaces exposed to the wind are covered by aeolian sand waves of diverse wavelengths, from centimetres for small ripples to decameters for dunes. Sand dunes can be said to be antifragile, since their growth is not prohibited by storms, whereas ripples and megaripples are fragile since they get flattened. The fluid-entrainment hypothesis attributes their fragility to a common cause: the spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment of grains. Here, we challenge this conventional view by revealing its major shortcomings and inconsistencies. An alternative framework, routed in the granular bed rheology, posits that impact ripples are erased when the two-phase flow of ballistically hopping grains on a solid sand surface gives way to a three-phase flow, featuring an intermediate, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. Notably, both martian wind-drag ripples and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, which emerge via a hydrodynamic instability, are insensitive to such "surface-melting". Their destruction is predicated on the transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions, instead. Our theoretical arguments are well supported by a stability diagram in terms of Shields number and grain diameter, assembled from a carefully reassessed large body of literature, and backed up by dedicated control measurements.

papers.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
papers.abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

papers.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(\beta_c(n)=\beta_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(\gamma_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/\beta_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

papers.title: La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity
papers.abstract: Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of $\sim 85$ kpc, has a long dimension of $\sim 57^\circ$ ($\sim 85$ kpc), and a width that varies from $\sim 10^\circ $ ($\sim 15$ kpc) to $\sim 35^\circ $ ($\sim 50$ kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by $\sim 35^\circ$ from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of $0.59$ days, and only $19\pm 3 \%$ lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and $1 \sigma$ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger \citep{chandra2023} is supported by the $\sim 70^\circ$ angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

papers.title: Origins of Satellite-System Building Blocks I: Solid Delivery During Jupiter's Growth
papers.abstract: Jupiter's satellites formed within a circumplanetary disk (CPD), but the origin and delivery of the solids from which they accreted remain uncertain. Here, we investigate the delivery of planetesimal material to the CPD while consistently accounting for the growth of Jupiter and the evolution of its surrounding planetesimal reservoir. Using N-body simulations coupled to an evolving CPD model, we quantify the solid mass supplied through planetesimal ablation and direct capture. We find that, although proto-Jupiter rapidly opens a gap in the planetesimal disk, planetesimals continue to enter the CPD for more than 1 Myr. Under efficient ablation, the mass deposited in the CPD can reach approximately 1 Me, about one order of magnitude higher than the mass delivered through direct capture. However, the low efficiency of pebble accretion within the CPD implies that forming the Galilean satellites from ablated material alone may require a very large pebble reservoir. Directly captured planetesimals, despite contributing less total mass, can instead provide satellitesimals that grow through mutual collisions and serve as seeds for subsequent pebble accretion. Our results therefore favor a hybrid formation pathway in which the Galilean satellites grow through a combination of satellitesimal and pebble accretion. We further demonstrate that even a planetesimal reservoir containing less solid material than the minimum-mass solar nebula can supply sufficient building blocks to form the Galilean satellites. The balance between the ablation and direct capture depends sensitively on the efficiency of aerodynamic heating: if ablation is weaker than commonly assumed, direct capture can become the dominant source of satellite building blocks. These results connect the formation of Jupiter and its satellites by showing how Jupiter's growth regulates both the duration and form of solid delivery to its CPD.

papers.title: Characterization of the mechanical vibrations of the Schmidt Camera at the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory
papers.abstract: Mechanical vibrations in astronomical telescopes can degrade image quality, making their detection and characterization essential. This work presents the development and validation of a low-cost, portable vibration monitoring system based on MEMS accelerometers interfaced with a microcontroller. The system integrates sensor acquisition and data analysis capabilities and was evaluated through controlled laboratory tests. The system was subsequently deployed at the historic Schmidt Camera of the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory in Mexico. After more than 80 years of operation, this study represents the first characterization of its mechanical vibrations. Preliminary measurements reveal dominant frequency components and their corresponding amplitudes, providing insight into the telescope's dynamic behavior and potential structural couplings that may affect image quality. Understanding the vibrational environment of astronomical telescopes is essential for the successful integration of new instrumentation. Identifying vibration frequencies and amplitudes can support the development of mitigation strategies, data filtering techniques, and numerical simulations to predict image quality degradation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of low-cost inertial sensing for monitoring heritage-class telescopes and provide a foundation for future instrumentation and preservation efforts at the Tonantzintla Observatory.

papers.title: A New Framework for Quantum Reinforcement Learning
SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots
papers.abstract: Soft robots built from active materials can directly convert environmental stimuli into motion, offering a route to energy autonomy and embodied control. However, environmental energy is generally harvested at low power, whereas rapid, mechanically demanding actions require high mechanical output power. Reconciling this mismatch while sustaining self-regulated cyclic actuation is challenging, particularly at the subgram scale, where limited payload capacity constrains the integration of conventional power and control hardware. Here, we present SunLightBots, a class of subgram, sunlight-powered, untethered soft robots that achieve autonomous locomotion under continuous illumination near 1 Sun (100 mW/cm2). Their operation is enabled by a self-resetting snapping (SRS) mechanism that integrates liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) with snap-through instability to accumulate solar energy supplied at low power, release it as rapid, high-power motion, and reset through photothermal-mechanical feedback. Through coordinated optimization of the LCE actuation temperature, photothermal conversion, actuation stress, and structural energy barrier, the system operates near 1 Sun and achieves a peak mass-specific mechanical power of 89 W/kg. At this irradiance, the optimized LCE generates an actuation stress of 0.1 MPa at approximately 60 deg C. SunLightBots demonstrate sustained swimming, crawling, and repeated impulsive jumping. Under 1.5 Suns, the swimmer advances more than three body lengths per cycle. This work provides a materials-mechanics route toward autonomous soft robots powered entirely by the environment.

papers.title: SyntheIce: A Synthetic Radargram Annotation Benchmark for Englacial Layer Reconstruction
Susceptibility Bottlenecks in Equilibrium Propagation Using Oscillator Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Equilibrium propagation (EP) enables learning in physical systems by exploiting the displacement between free and weakly perturbed equilibrium states. Here, we investigate how the underlying oscillator dynamics govern the transmission of learning signals in oscillator Ising machines (OIMs). We show that the hidden-layer response can be decomposed into two distinct factors: the nudging force applied at the output and the susceptibility governing its transmission to the hidden layer. Using a bipartite OIM with interactions interpolating between phase-difference and phase-sum coupling, we investigate these factors while ensuring that all coupling forms realize the same Ising Hamiltonian at binary phase-locked states. We demonstrate that second-harmonic injection primarily influences the nudging force through phase binarization, whereas the coupling form controls the cross-layer susceptibility through the mixed curvature of the energy landscape. At equal mixing, the mixed curvature vanishes on the binary manifold, strongly suppressing hidden-layer learning signals. Numerical simulations validate these mechanisms and reveal their consequences for classification performance. Our findings establish that realizing a desired energy landscape alone is insufficient to ensure effective physical learning; the system must also support the transmission of perturbations required for learning.

papers.title: Comparison of the flamelet progress variable and thickened flame models for LES of turbulent combustion
papers.abstract: Large-eddy simulation (LES) of turbulent combustion requires closure models for unresolved flame structures and chemical processes. Two widely used but fundamentally different approaches are the flamelet/progress-variable approach (FPVA) and the dynamically thickened-flame model (TFM). Here, both are applied to methane-air combustion within a common numerical framework and evaluated for the Sandia D flame and a jet-in-crossflow representative of a non-assist waste-gas flare across a range of crosswind-to-jet velocity ratios. For the predominantly diffusion-controlled Sandia-D flame, FPVA and TFM exhibit similar accuracy, while FPVA is substantially less computationally expensive and converges faster under mesh refinement. More detailed chemical kinetics improve agreement with experimental measurements, with little additional cost for FPVA but a substantial increase for TFM. For the jet-in-crossflow, both approaches reproduce the experimentally observed reduction in combustion efficiency with increasing crosswind, but their predictions progressively diverge as the crosswind strength increases. This divergence coincides with the emergence of a locally premixed reaction branch captured by TFM but not represented by FPVA, whereas predictions in diffusion-dominated regions remain broadly similar. In TFM, the locally premixed branch is associated with elevated scalar dissipation and greater residual methane downstream, indicating that highly strained premixed combustion contributes to differences in predicted flare performance. These results show that FPVA and TFM can provide similar predictions in diffusion-dominated flames but differ substantially when crossflow induces locally premixed, highly strained combustion near the nozzle.

papers.title: Harmony: Bridging Audio Understanding and Editing through Agentic Collaboration
The Gaia-alerted 2024--2025 brightening of V346 Nor
papers.abstract: Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass--accretion rate product $M_{\star}\dot{M}$ and the line-of-sight extinction $A_V$ are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher ($M_{\star}\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}^2\,$yr$^{-1}$) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from $A_V \approx 20$\,mag to $10$\,mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2\% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in H$\alpha$ indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

papers.title: Fatigue crack growth without plasticity under cyclically reversed shear
papers.abstract: We show that cyclic fatigue can occur in a system whose elements behave elastically up to an irreversible failure threshold, without plasticity, friction, or any time-dependent process. The model represents a weak interface between two elastic bodies loaded in shear. Under sufficiently large cyclic loading below the static failure threshold, a pre-existing flaw advances progressively, by a few lattice spacings per cycle. Two conditions are needed for this behavior: each bond fails more easily under one sense of the shear than the opposite, and the shear must be reversed during the cycle by an amount large enough to break bonds that have not yet failed. The model thus identifies the minimal conditions for an intrinsic, plasticity-free fatigue mechanism. Such conditions may be met at interfaces and weak planes subjected to strongly reversed shear, as in fretting, rolling contact, and reversed torsion, or in cyclic shear of cemented granular materials.

papers.title: Time Advances and Dispersive Constraints in Dressed Gravitational Scattering
papers.abstract: We derive a low energy group time advance in 4D dressed gravitational scattering at leading eikonal order with full soft dependence for a sharp dressing profile of finite soft scale. Dispersive matching of nonnegative absorption excludes the amplitude's analytic crossing with high energy boundedness. This reflects internal scales growing with energy via string diffusion in quantum gravity and high energy nonlinear graviton rescattering, coupled to soft clouds beyond leading soft order. Interference preserving joint detection of hard particles and coherent soft radiation may reveal the advance.

papers.title: Force-Dependent Change of Structural Behavior Upon Pulling a Grafted Flexible Polymer
papers.abstract: Manipulating polymer chains by means of experimental instruments such as optical tweezers has helped understand better the effects of molecular forces in macromolecular structures. In this study, we simulate the influence of a pulling force on structural phases of a coarse-grained model for flexible polymers using generalized-ensemble Monte Carlo methodologies. The recently introduced microcanonical inflection-point analysis method is employed to identify and classify structural phases of the system. Specific order parameters help characterize the transition behavior in response to the present pulling force. We show that, upon increasing the pulling strength, the coil-globule transition turns from second to first order, then merges with the liquid-solid transition. An intermediate phase, separating the coil and globule phases, is identified for certain force strengths. Clear evidence of the Gough-Joule effect is found as well. Transitions do not occur at all if the pulling force exceeds a certain threshold value.

papers.title: Martingale posteriors for flexible regression via recursive least squares
papers.abstract: Predictive Bayes quantifies uncertainty by specifying a sequence of one-step-ahead predictive distributions, inducing a martingale posterior without an explicit prior. Existing parametric constructions rely on stochastic-gradient updates and have seen limited development for flexible regression. We propose a predictive Bayes framework based on recursive least squares, whose martingale posterior has an explicit representation: given future covariates, it is the law of the posterior mean plus a weighted series of independent draws from the standardized predictive distribution. The posterior mean is a penalized least squares estimator, available in closed form and invariant to data ordering, whereas the predictive distribution, for example heavy tailed, is chosen separately without changing the estimator or algorithm. We derive the exact posterior variance under a known design and an asymptotically Gaussian approximation, and obtain the martingale posterior in closed form for Gaussian predictive distributions. Posterior draws are independent by construction, with a known truncation error, and require no Markov chain Monte Carlo. The construction extends to additive, mixed and Gaussian process models. In simulations and an analysis of NHANES triglyceride data, the method attains accuracy comparable to that of a fully Bayesian model with the same response distribution at a fraction of its computational cost.

papers.title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: Cross-Attribute Externalities of Fairness Interventions
A Three-Stage Unsupervised Online Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microgrid Optimal Power Flow
Robust Decoupled Input Filtering for Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
papers.abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.

papers.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
papers.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

papers.title: Methodological Pitfalls in Predicting Ship Turnaround Time at Brazilian Ports: An Empirical Audit and a Reproducible Pipeline
papers.abstract: Two recent studies on ship turnaround time at Brazilian ports report models with R-squared scores above 0.80 on data from the national waterway transportation agency. We audit their published datasets and reveal these results are inflated by structural data leakage. Specifically, 97 percent of berthing events in their random row-level split appear in both training and testing partitions. We demonstrate that a model's R-squared drops from 0.82 to 0.20 when the data is properly split at the berthing level. We further document additional methodological flaws, including survivorship bias, undocumented target truncation, and the retention of variables that algebraically reconstruct the target. To address these issues, we propose a reproducible pipeline that aggregates cargo to the berthing level, utilizes conditional imputation, and represents high-cardinality cargo variables through weighted averages of multilingual sentence embeddings. Evaluating six time targets and thirty seeds, our pipeline reveals that cargo embeddings yield statistically significant improvements on four operational targets, while administrative waiting times remain unaffected. Prior works missed this per-target heterogeneity by conflating genuine signal with leaked identity.

papers.title: Joint Beamforming and Duplex-Mode Segment Selection for Secure Uplink Transmission in Pinching Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have recently emerged as a promising architecture for reconfigurable, flexible and proximity-driven signal delivery. In this paper, we propose a segmented waveguide-based PASS architecture for enabling secure uplink communications, where each segment activates at most one pinching antenna (PA), which inherently eliminates the inter-antenna re-radiation effect and yields a tractable uplink signal model. To protect the uplink transmission against eavesdropping, the base station (BS) injects artificial noise (AN) toward the eavesdroppers via selected downlink segments using a duplex-mode segment selection mechanism, which dynamically configures each segment for either uplink reception or downlink AN transmission through switch-controlled fiber connections. We formulate the secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes the receive beamforming vector, AN covariance, user transmit power, pinching antenna positions, and duplex-mode segment assignment. Given the non-convex and combinatorial nature of the problem, we develop an efficient alternating optimization (AO) framework, where the resulting subproblems are solved using the Dinkelbach method combined with successive convex approximation (SCA) and penalty-based relaxation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of SEE and robustness against waveguide attenuation. Moreover, AN effectively suppresses information leakage, while PA mobility, duplex-mode segment allocation, and waveguide segmentation further improve secrecy performance through flexible positioning and reduced in-waveguide propagation loss.

papers.title: Symmetry adapted tensor networks and quantum classical geometric learning for hadronic tomography: a proton construction
papers.abstract: We construct a calibrated model of the proton generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distribution (GTMD) $F_{1,1}$ in the real, staple-even valence-$u$ sector at zero skewness. Experimental measurements, lattice matrix elements, and phenomenological distributions enter through a single shared light-front state, organized as a symmetry-resolved tree tensor network in which color-singlet structure, exchange statistics, and the additive $J_z$ and $I_z$ charges are built in. Classical and quantum geometric nodes represent the residual transverse response. The GTMD is defined with soft subtraction, one-loop nonsinglet matching, NLO collinear evolution, and an explicit nonperturbative joint closure, so that each input is used with its own operator convention and scale. Calibrating against correlated ART25 transverse projections, HERA inclusive data, and lattice, elastic, and static information gives a simple picture. The forward inputs narrow the attainable transverse response by about $81\%$ at $x=0.4$. The simultaneous dependence on quark momentum and momentum transfer, however, is untouched by any of them: a deformation that leaves every present input invariant moves the nonforward value from $0.588$ to $0.378\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$. Dense momentum-space surfaces and finite-transfer-window phase-space maps show the structure this freedom controls. The tensor-network organization is chosen with composition in mind. The same shared subunits, operator hierarchy, and qualification protocol extend to the neutron, the spin-1 deuteron, and spin-$3/2$ nuclei, where the number of symmetry and exchange constraints grows quickly and a structural representation becomes the practical route. The quantum circuits are verified feature maps and state encodings; their capacity and cost are measured alongside the classical blocks.

papers.title: MAGI (Multivariate Autoencoder for particle Generative Inference): a generative Machine Learning framework for accelerated multi-stage particle simulations
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo particle simulations are hindered by the computational cost of particle transport. This is especially true when large mass surrounds a small sensitive volume. MAGI is a conditional variational autoencoder that learns the joint energy, position and direction distribution of particles crossing a closed surface in a multi-stage simulation, to be resampled and re-injected in a smaller mass model. We validated it generating crossings, variables describing particle features later in the simulation, injecting them into the same Geant4 mass model and comparing the spectrum and counts at detector level with full simulation. Rates per injected crossing agree with unity at $\sim1\sigma$ on our benchmark models. We measure the gain of MAGI with statistical amplification $1/\chi$ and computational speed-up $S$: the first goes from 150 for high-statistics cosmic rays to 12000 for rare radioactive decays, while the latter ranges from 2.1 to almost 240, depending on source type and mass model. These first results validate MAGI v1.0.0 released on GitHub.

papers.title: Deep Unrolling of Lanczos-based Laplacian Eigensolver for Crop Classification in Satellite Images
papers.abstract: Per-pixel crop classification in satellite images is an important pre-processing step in remote crop monitoring. Leveraging progress in signed graph signal processing, we build an interpretable and lightweight neural network for binary crop classification (e.g., corn versus non-corn) in two stages: i) learn a signed graph from data, and ii) unroll a Lanczos-based eigensolver to compute the eigenvector $\u_1$ associated with the smallest eigenvalue of a hybrid graph Laplacian $\cL$ for spectral clustering. Specifically, we first construct a near-balanced signed graph $\cG^s$, where signed edge weights $w_{i,j}\in(-1,1)$ are computed from learned feature distances $d_{i,j}$ via a hyperbolic tangent mapping. Given $\cG^s$, we estimate $\u_1$ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use $\mathrm{sign}(\u_1)$ for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which $\u_1$ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age
Relativistic Second Random-Phase Approximation: Formalism and Applications to Giant Resonances
papers.abstract: We develop a self-consistent relativistic second random-phase approximation (RSRPA) based on covariant energy density functional with density dependent point-coupling interaction. The formalism extends the conventional simple configuration space composed of particle-hole ($p$-$h$) transitions by including two-particle-two-hole ($2p$-$2h$) configurations through a generalized Thouless ansatz and a time-dependent variational principle. To ensure consistency with the underlying mean-field ground state and avoid the double counting of correlations, we implement the subtraction method, in which the static contribution is removed from the residual interaction. The first applications of the RSRPA include studies of isoscalar and isovector giant monopole (ISGMR and IVGMR) and quadrupole resonances (ISGQR and IVGQR) in $^{16}$O, which demonstrate the importance of $2p$-$2h$ couplings to describe the fragmentation of the transition strength and the stabilizing role of the subtraction method.

papers.title: Beyond Foreign-Key Connectivity: Semantic Relationship Representation for Relational Deep Learning
Improving Airflow Network Models of Natural Ventilation: Geometry-Specific Pressures and Fluctuation Corrections
papers.abstract: Building energy models typically predict natural ventilation rates using airflow networks, which solve a system of orifice equations with exterior pressures as boundary conditions. This study investigates two improvements to these models: (i) geometry-specific exterior pressures obtained from large eddy simulations (LESs) and (ii) analytical corrections accounting for the nonlinear effects of pressure fluctuations on mean ventilation rates. We evaluate these improvements against coupled interior-exterior LESs of flows through 5824 windows, 2688 skylights, and 2752 interiors across idealized urban canopies. Replacing standard ASHRAE pressure coefficients with pressures from exterior-only LESs reduces the RMSE of predicted ventilation rates by approximately 50%, largely by capturing urban canopy flow effects that are poorly represented by standard shelter factors. Independently of the pressure source, mean-pressure airflow network predictions exhibit a nonlinear relationship with the LES ventilation rates. To address this discrepancy, we derive fluctuation corrections for mean-dominated and fluctuation-dominated flow regimes. These corrections eliminate the systematic nonlinearity and further reduce RMSE by 10-40% for most opening types and ventilation configurations. For windows, the combined improvements from geometry-specific surface pressures and fluctuation corrections increase the coefficient of determination $R^2$ from approximately 0.4 to 0.9. The results demonstrate the potential to accurately predict natural ventilation rates across different interior layouts while accounting for urban canopy effects and pressure fluctuations, using exterior-only LES pressure information.

papers.title: Code as Explanations: Executable and Verifiable LLM Explanations

Dwarfs of Fire and Ice: UV-Irradiation-Driven Thermal Inversion, Disequilibrium Chemistry, and a Cloud-Free Atmosphere in a Strongly Irradiated Brown Dwarf Probed by JWST/NIRSpec Phase-Resolved Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We present time-resolved JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectrophotometry of the white dwarf (WD)-brown dwarf (BD) binary SDSS J141126.20+200911.1 (SDSS1411). Close WD-BD binaries provide powerful laboratories for studying the effects of stellar irradiation on substellar atmospheres because of their high companion-to-host flux ratios, short orbital periods, and intense UV irradiation from the WD. We measure strong wavelength-dependent variability, with day-night relative flux variations reaching ~280%. The SDSS1411B phase curves are well described by a second-order Fourier model, and correlations among the Fourier amplitudes suggest larger flux and temperature variations in the upper atmosphere. Non-irradiated forward models under chemical equilibrium do not reproduce the observed phase-resolved SDSS1411B spectra, indicating substantial departures from isolated-BD atmospheric structures. In contrast, atmospheric retrievals successfully reproduce both the dayside and nightside spectra. The retrievals reveal a prominent dayside temperature inversion, favor cloud-free atmospheres, and provide evidence for CO2 disequilibrium chemistry. An energy-budget analysis indicates low day-to-night heat redistribution efficiency and constrains the BD cooling age to ~3 Gyr, while the inferred BD radius is significantly more compact than predicted by BD evolutionary models. These results reveal the rich atmospheric dynamics and disequilibrium chemistry of a UV-irradiated BD and demonstrate the power of full-orbit JWST phase-resolved spectroscopy for constraining the atmospheric physics of strongly irradiated substellar objects.

papers.title: Chaotic-Periodic Alternation in a Financial System with Double Delays
papers.abstract: In this paper we present the chaotic-periodic alternation phenomenon within a three-dimensional nonlinear financial system subjected to Pyragas-type time-delayed feedback, as well as the lag effect of the interest rate in the price index dynamics. Through numerical analysis, transitions to chaos, including period-doubling cascades, period-halving routes, and incommensurable-period dynamics are characterized. The emergence of chaotic-periodic alternation are found and described. Results suggest that minor timing misalignments in the inner dynamics of a financial system, as well as those considered in the feedback loop can induce systemic volatility.

papers.title: DIISC-VIII: Chemical Signatures of Gas Accretion in Star-Forming Galaxies
authors: Timothy M. Heckman (1 and 5) ((1) School of Earth and Space Exploration
papers.abstract: We investigate anomalously low-metallicity (ALM) star-forming regions in 11 galaxies from the Deciphering the Interplay between the Interstellar Medium, Stars, and the Circumgalactic Medium (DIISC) survey. We combine optical spectroscopy of 542 H$\alpha$-bright regions from MMT/Binospec with imaging from the Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope and H I 21 cm imaging from the Very Large Array. We find 75 ALM regions: 19 identified using deviations from each galaxy's radial metallicity gradient, 27 using the resolved mass--metallicity relation (rMZR), and 29 via both methods. Regions identified by both methods are metal-poor relative to their galactocentric positions and local stellar mass surface densities by $>$ 0.1 dex, making them the strongest candidates for localized metallicity dilution. We estimate accreted masses of $5.6<\log(M_{\rm acc}/{\rm M_\odot})<7.5$ for the 48 radial-gradient-selected regions, comparable to observed and simulated high-velocity cloud masses. We calculate a mean hydrogen accretion rate of $1.02\ {\rm M_\odot yr^{-1}}$ per galaxy, which is comparable to the mean star formation rate of the sample. The strongest ALM candidates lie within or near $R_{25}$, while rMZR-only regions dominate the outer population. We find no evidence that circumgalactic Ly$\alpha$ absorption along a single sightline traces disk chemical structure, as quantified by either the radial metallicity gradient or the fraction of radial-gradient-selected ALM regions. These results suggest that localized accretion of low-metallicity gas can sustain star formation in galaxies and demonstrate that ALM regions provide a spatially resolved indirect view of ongoing gas cycling.

papers.title: Probe What-If Worlds Before You Ship: Persona Simulation for Real-World Decision Making
Conformal Risk Certificates for Portfolio Optimization Under Uncertainty: A Gated Reinforcement-Learning Approach
Incrementally Verifiable Oracle Aided Computation
Beyond Row-Level Prediction: Evaluating and Learning Composition for Reusable Table Representations
Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
Faithful filtering of constrained quantum records: Local limits and collective advantage from loops
papers.abstract: Weak probes can record whether neighboring spins are aligned without revealing their common orientation. Reading the probes can then herald a projection of an unknown spin state onto the aligned subspace that preserves every coherence within it. We ask how often this projection succeeds when the probes are read separately or jointly. For binary pure product records and zero false positives, we derive the exact optimum over all separable measurements, and hence over all local operations and classical communication. It is the probability that one-sided local witnesses exclude every alternative, and simultaneous local measurements attain it. Joint readout can do better by accepting coherent combinations of ambiguous outcomes in which the alternatives cancel. For pairwise parity records on a connected simple graph, it beats every local strategy exactly when the graph has a loop, at all record overlaps strictly between zero and one. For general binary linear records, the condition is an irreducible dependency among at least three records. The advantage lowers the leading power of the efficiency at weak recording. On a triangle the efficiency becomes linear rather than quadratic in the witness probability, and a three-pulse coherent-light receiver captures this gain with a single click. Extensions treat targets spanning several patterns and a noisy comparison at a common output fidelity.

papers.title: Real positive definite counterexamples to a monotonicity conjecture for the $q$-permanent
papers.abstract: The $q$-permanent $P_q$ of an $n\times n$ matrix weights the term of each permutation $\sigma$ by $q^{\inv(\sigma)}$, where $\inv(\sigma)$ is the number of inversions of $\sigma$. It interpolates between the determinant ($q=-1$) and the permanent ($q=1$). Extending a conjecture of Bapat on $[-1,1]$, it was conjectured in 2010 that the $q$-permanent of every non-diagonal real symmetric positive definite matrix is strictly increasing on an interval $(\varepsilon,+\infty)$ with $\varepsilon<-1$. In this note, we disprove this conjecture. An explicit real symmetric positive definite integer matrix of order five, whose $q$-permanent has only nine nonzero terms, satisfies $P_{14}(A)>P_{15}(A)$. A sparse family shows that for every real $r>1$ some real symmetric positive definite matrix has a $q$-permanent with negative derivative at $q=r$. The counterexamples can be chosen to be correlation matrices without zero entries or, separately, to have integer entries. We also show that the smallest order of a counterexample is four, and that matrices supported on three coordinates separated by identity blocks fail much closer to $q=1$: in order five already near $q=1.7$, and in order $O(1/(r-1))$ at any prescribed $q=r>1$.

papers.title: Correlation Geometry and Emergent Space-Time from Stochastic Correlation Flows
papers.abstract: We propose an effective framework relating correlation geometry to stochastic flows of correlation projectors. Physical configurations are encoded by measures on spaces of self-adjoint operators, with physical equivalence defined by unitary conjugation. Assuming a smooth, spectrally separated correlation sector, local orthonormal frames define a Wilczek--Zee connection, while a Stratonovich gradient-flow ansatz preserves the projector constraints. In a local continuum approximation with massive fast modes, standard one-loop methods generate Yang--Mills-type terms and curvature terms of Einstein--Hilbert form. Along a smooth closed path, the trace of a cyclic product of projectors converges to the trace of the parallel-transport operator as the discretization is refined. We examine possible geometric, disordered, and topological regimes and motivate the stochastic dynamics through an effective open-system description. The first-order frame action defines a symplectic structure on the projector sector, providing a starting point for its relation to gravitational canonical variables. We identify the matching conditions required for an Ashtekar phase-space description and the assumptions connecting correlation geometry to induced interactions and emergent spacetime.

papers.title: Steady-state of Lévy process with general resetting: unreflected and reflected cases
papers.abstract: We study (unreflected and reflected) Lévy processes that are modified at independent Poisson review epochs by a random state-dependent reset map. The first model is unreflected: between resettings the level evolves as a Lévy process, and at a resetting epoch the new level is $F$ of the level seen just before the resetting. The second model is the reflected Lévy process at $0$, but with reset maps chosen from a wider transform-solvable class. In this work, we give contraction-type ergodicity criteria for the existence of the steady-state. We identify this steady-state of the system as the solution of certain stochastic fixed-point equation. This allows to find the Laplace-transform, moments recursions, and regularly-varying-tail formulae. For non-reflected case, the examples include affine deterministic resets $F(x)=cx+b$, random-coefficient resets $F(x)=Cx+b$ with two-point $C$ for the finite-activity Lévy process, spectrally positive Lévy flight, reflected Brownian process. For the reflected cased we analyse affine resetting mechanism $F(x)=cx$, the alternating resetting $F(x)=(B-x)^+$, and uniform proportional resetting $F(x)=Cx$ with $C$ having uniform distribution.

papers.title: Symplectic capacities of 4-dimensional monotone toric domains
papers.abstract: We compute the cylindrical contact homology chain complex associated with a monotone toric domain in $\mathbb{R}^4$. The chain complexes allow us to compute the cylindrical contact homology capacities associated with monotone toric domains with one or two inflection points. These capacities are conjecturally equal to the Gutt-Hutchings capacities defined using $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. Using our results, we find embedding obstructions between toric domains.

papers.title: Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems
papers.abstract: Gaia DR4 will, for the first time, provide epoch astrometry. When analysing these data, binary sources must be treated carefully, as modelling their astrometry as single stars can bias parallax and proper motion estimates. We developed the vimbinary tool, a framework to simulate and interpret epoch astrometry of unresolved binary systems and to evaluate the impact of model assumptions on the resulting astrometric parameters. We simulated Gaia DR4-like epoch astrometry for a sample of 17 well-characterised unresolved binary systems, including both non-pulsating binaries and systems containing one photometric variable component - variability-induced movers (VIMs). We show that both binary motion and the VIM effect can significantly impact parallax and proper motion measurements, with the magnitude of the effect strongly dependent on the orbital period, photocentric amplitude, and flux ratio of the specific system. We also show that larger time coverage does not necessarily improve parallax precision, in contrast to proper motion, for which precision generally improves with longer baselines. Instead, parallaxes retrieved with binary-system fitting are more accurate than those obtained within the single-star framework.

papers.title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$. Deleting four lines then produces a thirteen-line arrangement whose second Chern class is controlled by a combinatorial deficit. When the deficit is four, the remaining arrangement is free with exponents $(6,6)$. An exact covering argument places the necessary thirteen-line cores in four finite classes, containing $3{,}829{,}691$ lattices. We compute their realisation spaces and reconstruct all relevant seventeen-line extensions, including specialisations of positive-dimensional families. Among the candidate lattices, exactly sixteen admit a non-free realisation; they are rigid and have no free realisation. Together with the known cases, this establishes Terao's conjecture for central arrangements of at most seventeen planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$.

papers.title: Anatomy of AdS black hole on-shell actions
papers.abstract: We revisit the regularized on-shell actions of rotating electrically charged AdS black holes of gauged supergravity via holographic renormalization and background subtraction, with a particular emphasis on the frame in which the radial cutoff is placed.
